chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Najjah, who said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us from Amr ibn Kathir al-Sarraj al-Nahwi from Abu al-Jarud from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He asked me, 'How far is it between you and Husain (peace be upon him)?' I said, 'A day for the rider, and a day and a part for the walker.' He asked, 'Do you visit him every Friday?' I said, 'No, I only visit him on the two Fridays.' He said, ' You are far off (negligent). If it were near us, we would make it a Hijrah (migration), meaning we would migrate to it.

key_terms.الْجُمُعَتَیْنِ: the two Fridays (a specific period or dual Fridays)
key_terms.الْحُسَیْن: Imam Husain (peace be upon him), grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.لِلرَّاکِبِ: for the rider (referring to travel time by mount)
key_terms.لِلْمَاشِی: for the walker (referring to travel time on foot)
key_terms.هِجْرَهً: migration, implying a significant relocation for the sake of a sacred place

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam Husain according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the spiritual gravity of Ziyarat by using the metaphor of Hijrah (migration) to illustrate that proximity to the Imam’s grave warrants constant devotion. Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) critiques Abu al-Jarud’s infrequent visits, noting that if the shrine were physically closer, the companions would have made it their primary residence, thereby elevating Ziyarat from a ritual act to a central pillar of Shia spiritual life.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 19.  Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) asked Abul Jarud, “How far is the grave of Imam Husain (a.s.) from your house?” He replied, “If I go on a mount it takes a day to reach and if I walk, it takes a little more than that.” Imam asked, “Do you go  for  Ziyarat  every  Friday?”  He  replied,  “No,  but  I  go whenever  I  get  time.”  Imam  said,  “You  are  unjust.  If  this place  would  have  been  near  my  home  I  would  have migrated over there.”
